candidate.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows

evidence.text: A key design element of Swin Transformer is its shift of the window partition between consecutive self-attention layers, as illustrated in Figure 2. The shifted windows bridge the windows of the preceding layer, providing connections among them that significantly enhance modeling power (see Table 4). This strategy is also efficient in regards to real-world latency: all query patches within a window share the same key set 1, which facilitates memory access in hardware. In contrast, earlier sliding window based self-attention approaches [33, 50] suffer from low latency on general hardware due to different key sets for different query pixels 2. Our experiments show that the proposed shifted window approach has much lower latency than the sliding window method, yet is similar in modeling power (see Tables 5 and 6). The shifted window approach also proves beneficial for all-MLP architectures [61].
